title_en: Jiangsu First Construction Installation Group Co., Ltd. v. Tangshan Changlong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project construction contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 21 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Contracts provides that where the parties conclude another construction contract for the same project which substantially differs from the filed contract awarded through a public tender, the filed contract shall serve as the basis for settling the project price. However, the prerequisite for applying this provision is that the filed contract is lawful and valid. An invalid filed contract does not automatically have priority over other invalid contracts as a reference for application.

full_text_en:
Jiangsu First Construction and Installation Group Co., Ltd. v. Tangshan Changlong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over construction project construction contract

【Ruling Summary】

Article 21 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts provides that where the parties enter into a separate construction project construction contract for the same project that materially differs in substantive content from the tendered contract that has been filed for record, the tendered contract that has been filed shall be used as the basis for settling the project price. The prerequisite for its application is that the filed tendered contract is legal and valid; an invalid filed contract does not inherently have priority over other invalid contracts for reference and application.

Where there are multiple construction contracts between the parties and all are invalid, generally the contract that reflects the true intention of the parties and has been actually performed should be referred to as the basis for settling the project price. Where the actually performed contract cannot be determined, a reasonable distribution may be made based on the price difference between the two disputed contracts, taking into account factors such as project quality, fault of the parties, and the principle of good faith.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Zhong No. 175

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant): Jiangsu First Construction and Installation Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Building 1, No. 2 Zidong Road, Qixia District, Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Minxiang, Chairman of the Company.

Agent Ad Litem: Ai Haifeng, Attorney at Beijing Zhongzhou Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Ren Shiguang, Attorney at Beijing Zhongzhou Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff): Tangshan Changlong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 107 Jianshe North Road, High-tech Development Zone, Tangshan City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Niu Jinfang, Chairman of the Company.

Agent Ad Litem: Ma Hongbin, Attorney at Hebei Binli Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Luo Zhanyi, Attorney at Beijing Zhaoyi Law Firm.

The appellant, Jiangsu First Construction and Installation Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiangsu First Construction), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2013) Ji Min Yi Chu Zi No. 17 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court in a dispute over a construction project construction contract with the respondent, Tangshan Changlong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changlong Company). After this Court accepted the case on March 20, 2017, a collegial panel was formed in accordance with the law and a hearing was held. Ai Haifeng and Ren Shiguang, agents ad litem of Jiangsu First Construction, and Ma Hongbin and Luo Zhanyi, agents ad litem of Changlong Company, appeared in court for the hearing. The case has now been concluded.

Jiangsu First Construction's appeal requests: (1) to set aside the civil judgment (2013) Ji Min Yi Chu Zi No. 17 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court; (2) to amend the judgment to order Changlong Company to pay the outstanding project amount of RMB 25,914,315.58, plus interest calculated at the loan interest rate of the same period announced by the People's Bank of China from January 30, 2012 until the date of full payment; (3) to amend the judgment to order Changlong Company to pay losses of RMB 3,750,000 for work stoppage and idling; (4) to amend the judgment to order Jiangsu First Construction to deliver all construction documents to Changlong Company within 15 days after Changlong Company pays all outstanding amounts; (5) to have the litigation costs of this case borne by Changlong Company. The facts and reasons are as follows:

(1) The first-instance judgment erred in its determination of the amount of outstanding project payment owed by Changlong Company and the calculation of interest.

The Construction Project Construction Contract (hereinafter referred to as the "Filed Contract") and the Golden He Yuan Construction and Installation Engineering Supplemental Agreement (hereinafter referred to as the "Supplemental Agreement") are both invalid and are not a "black-and-white contract." The Filed Contract is invalid due to its violation of tendering and bidding laws. The actual performance between the parties was carried out under the Supplemental Agreement, which reflects the true intention of both parties. The actual contract performed is the Supplemental Agreement, as evidenced by aspects such as the scope of the project, start and completion dates, settlement method, and supply of materials and equipment. Moreover, Changlong Company itself admitted that the Supplemental Agreement was a refinement and supplement to the Filed Contract.

The amount of project payment should not be determined by the validity of the contract but by whether the project quality is acceptable. Since both contracts in this case are invalid, settlement should be based on the actual quantity of work performed. The expert conclusion of RMB 150 million should be taken as the amount of project payment for actual settlement, serving as the basis for settlement and for paying interest on the outstanding project amount. The price difference between the two contracts is not a loss; rather, it is the actual project cost of the contractor. The proportional sharing of losses is improper.

The project in this case passed final acceptance inspection and was delivered for use on November 20, 2011. Referring to the Interim Measures for the Settlement of Construction Project Prices, which provides that settlement should be completed within 60 days, Changlong Company should, at the latest, have started paying interest on January 30, 2012, which is 60 days after the completion date.

(2) Changlong Company should compensate Jiangsu First Construction for idle work losses based on the actual labor and machinery costs incurred. This evidence consists of accounting books and records, which are authentic and complete. The first-instance court did not conduct an appraisal of the idle work losses, and Changlong Company also did not submit evidence to rebut them. Therefore, this should be determined accordingly.

(3) With respect to the quality issue concerning the staircase insulation of the project, the first-instance court's decision not to address the corresponding portion of the project payment is erroneous. These costs have not actually been incurred. Even if there is a quality problem, Jiangsu First Construction could be notified to carry out repairs. If Changlong Company has paid costs in advance, it can pursue another case separately.

(4) The first-instance court's order to deliver all construction documents to Changlong Company is erroneous. According to Articles 49 and 16 of the Regulations on the Quality Management of Construction Projects, Jiangsu First Construction's documents already meet the requirements. The failure to submit the documents was due to the incomplete documents from Changlong Company's independent subcontractors. Moreover, from the perspective of the right of defense based on insecurity, since Changlong Company has failed to settle and pay the project amount in a timely manner, Jiangsu First Construction is entitled to withhold the acceptance inspection documents.

Changlong Company argued in defense: The Filed Contract is the principal contract and the one actually performed by both parties. The Supplemental Agreement refined and confirmed the contents of the Filed Contract without making any material changes. Therefore, the Filed Contract should be used as the basis for settling the project price. The warranty obligations, inspection of concealed works in progress, construction organization and schedule, and installation works stipulated in the Filed Contract were not provided for in the Supplemental Agreement. Jiangsu First Construction's scope of work did not correspond to the scope specified in the Supplemental Agreement. For example, the main loop road project of the residential quarter, although within the scope of the Supplemental Agreement, was completed by another unit. The settlement method in the Supplemental Agreement changed the provisions of the Filed Contract. The first-instance judgment was clear in its findings of fact, correct in its application of law, and should be upheld, and Jiangsu First Construction's appeal should be dismissed. The first-instance judgment's order that Changlong Company bear 60% of the responsibility is excessive. The payment of interest should be premised on the existence of an accurate principal amount and a reasonable starting date for calculation. Jiangsu First Construction continued to submit supplementary settlement documents as late as February 2015, preventing the employer from conducting a final accounting, and the completion acceptance filing procedures have not been completed. The first-instance judgment calculated interest from the date the lawsuit was filed, and Changlong Company accepts this result. With respect to the idle work losses, Jiangsu First Construction has engaged in the fabrication of evidence and false statements; the documents issued do not comply with the procedures for determination, lack the signature of Changlong Company, and the fact of an 81-day work stoppage is not supported by relevant evidence. Although Changlong Company accepts the judgment, it hopes that the second-instance court will ascertain the facts. The project delivered by Jiangsu First Construction has quality issues that do not meet the design requirements. The first-instance court's decision not to address the corresponding portion of the project payment at this stage is in accordance with the law. The first-instance judgment ordering Jiangsu First Construction to deliver the construction documents is in accordance with the law.

Jiangsu First Construction's first-instance claim requested: (1) An order that Changlong Company pay the outstanding project amount of RMB 43,152,301 (subject to the amount determined by judicial appraisal) and interest on the delayed payment calculated at the loan interest rate of the same period announced by the People's Bank of China from the date of completion until the expiry of the performance period specified in the effective judgment (estimated at approximately RMB 6,040,160.69 for the purpose of calculating litigation costs). (2) An order that Changlong Company compensate for losses of RMB 3,750,000 from work stoppage and idling (subject to the amount determined by judicial appraisal). (3) The litigation costs of this case to be borne by Changlong Company.

Changlong Company's counterclaim requested: (1) An order that Jiangsu First Construction compensate for interest of RMB 1,282,000 on the overpaid project amount; (2) Delivery of documents for completion acceptance filing; (3) Compensation for losses of RMB 12,061,200 (RMB 10,779,200 + RMB 1,282,000) suffered by Changlong Company due to delayed delivery of completion acceptance documents, including financing losses; (4) Compensation for losses of RMB 228,300 paid by Changlong Company to small homeowners due to project quality issues; (5) An order that Jiangsu First Construction carry out rectification within a specified period for the insulation of staircases and corridors not subject to heating, the insulation of walls between residential units and corridors, and the insulation of main pipes in heating pipe shafts that do not comply with mandatory quality standards, and that Changlong Company temporarily withhold payment for that portion of the project; (6) The litigation costs of this case to be borne by Jiangsu First Construction.

The first-instance court found the following facts: Prior to signing the construction contract, Changlong Company, as the employer, and Jiangsu First Construction, as the contractor, signed the "Golden He Yuan Foundation Pit Support Contract," entrusting Jiangsu First Construction with the foundation pit support work for the Golden He Yuan project. The contract did not specify the date of signing.

On September 28, 2009, Jiangsu First Construction, Changlong Company, the design unit, and the supervision unit conducted a four-party review of the structural and electrical construction drawings for the project in question. Before the tendering and bidding procedures were carried out, Jiangsu First Construction had already completed some of the construction work, including positioning surveys, foundation marking, and foundation blinding for some of the buildings in the project.

On December 1, 2009, following tendering and bidding procedures, Changlong Company determined Jiangsu First Construction as the successful bidder for the Golden He Yuan residential project it was developing and issued a "Letter of Acceptance" to Jiangsu First Construction. Changlong Company's bidding documents indicated that the contract price would be determined on a fixed total price basis. On December 8, 2009, the parties signed the "Filed Contract," which stipulated that Jiangsu First Construction would contract for the construction of the Golden He Yuan residential project developed by Changlong Company, with a total floor area of 110,998 square meters, and the scope of the work included the construction and installation of all civil works, plumbing and heating, electrical, elevator, fire protection, and ventilation works as indicated in the construction drawings; the start date was December 8, 2009, the completion date was December 7, 2011, with a total contract period of 730 calendar days; the contract price was RMB 131,839,227.62. In Section 23.2 of the Special Terms of the contract, it originally stated: "The contract price is determined on an adjustable price contract basis. The adjustment method for the contract price is: settlement based on construction drawings, material price adjustments, design changes, and on-site variations to be adjusted according to actual conditions, implementing the Hebei Province 2008 Budget Quota for Construction and Installation Works and the agreements or stipulations of both parties." Subsequently, the parties crossed out this provision and changed it to: "The contract price is determined on a fixed total price basis," "All items are included in the total contract price except for design changes and on-site variations," and "The adjustment method for contract price outside the scope of risk is to be adjusted by a total price reduction of 3% based on three-party certifications by the employer, contractor, and supervision unit." The places where the corrections were made were all stamped with the seals of both parties. Section 28.1 of the Special Terms stipulated that "Materials and equipment purchased by the contractor shall comply with national standards and design requirements. The quality and price of major materials and new materials shall be confirmed by the employer." This agreement was filed with the Tangshan Construction Bureau on December 30, 2009.

On December 28, 2009, the parties signed the "Supplemental Agreement," which stated that it was a clarification of the relevant supplementary terms of the Golden He Yuan construction project construction contract, serving as an appendix to the principal contract and having the same legal effect as the principal contract. Article 1 of this agreement stipulated that the contract start and completion dates were from September 30, 2009 to September 15, 2011; Article 3 stipulated that the basis for contracting was the Golden He Yuan construction drawings designed by China Beijing Design and Research Institute, after review and submission for clarification, the change specifications (Appendix 1), the scope of confirmation of quality and price for major materials (Appendix 2), and the current national, provincial, and municipal regulations and standards for construction inspection; Article 4 stipulated the settlement method: This project implements the Hebei Province 2008 Quota and related documents; the total construction and installation cost settlement amount is reduced by 3%. During the construction and acceptance phases, the provisional price is used as the basis for payment. For 18-story residential buildings, the provisional price for the above-ground portion is RMB 1,200 per square meter; for residential buildings below 18 stories, the provisional price for the above-ground portion is RMB 1,000 per square meter; for the underground portion (including civil air defense), the provisional price is RMB 1,625 per square meter. Article 5 stipulated price adjustments: Major materials for this project are subject to quality and price confirmation by Party A (see Appendix 2 for the scope of quality and price confirmation). Party B shall submit a material plan in advance. Before materials arrive at the site, Party A shall confirm the material prices. After materials arrive at the site, Party A, Party B and the supervision unit shall jointly confirm the quantity of materials received. The price shall be based on Party A's price confirmation order. The materials delivered to the site must comply with current standard requirements and design requirements. The price shall be confirmed by Party A and shall be based on the newly issued price confirmation order. The quantity of materials involved and the scope of the work shall be jointly confirmed by Party A, Party B and the supervision unit. Costs for construction organization design are not included in the final settlement. For main structure construction formwork, large formwork and bamboo plywood formwork shall be used. Design changes, project negotiations, and on-site variations shall be based on the signed approval documents from Party A. For individual changes with a total price of RMB 1,000 or less, no fee shall be charged, and Party B shall carry out the work unconditionally. For individual changes with a total price exceeding RMB 1,000, corresponding adjustments shall be made based on the 2008 Quota. Major material prices shall be based on the price confirmation orders of Party A at the same time. Transportation costs, procurement, and storage fees for price-confirmed materials shall be levied in accordance with regulations (except where transportation costs are already included in the confirmed price). Additionally, the agreement stipulated matters such as project payment and liability for breach of contract.

On November 30, 2011, the project undertaken by Jiangsu First Construction passed final acceptance inspection and was accepted. By the end of August 2012, Jiangsu First Construction submitted a complete settlement report to Changlong Company, which was acknowledged by Changlong Company.

Both parties acknowledged that during the construction process, except for the payment for the foundation pit support work, Changlong Company had paid Jiangsu First Construction RMB 124,939,155 in project payments. The amount for the foundation pit support work was RMB 700,963.84, which had been paid in full. However, since the foundation pit support project was a separate contract and was not within the scope of the cost audit for this case, the RMB 700,963.84 was also not included in the payments already made in this case.

During the proceedings, Jiangsu First Construction applied to the first-instance court for a cost appraisal of the project in question. The first-instance court, through its Judicial Technical Assistance Office, selected Hebei Jichengxiang Engineering Cost Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jichengxiang Company) as the appraisal institution in accordance with statutory procedures. Given the significant dispute between the parties over which contract should be used as the basis for appraising the project price—Changlong Company advocated settlement based on the fixed total price method stipulated in the filed contract, while Jiangsu First Construction advocated settlement based on the adjustable price method stipulated in the supplemental agreement—the first-instance court instructed the appraisal institution to conduct appraisals based on both contracts separately, as claimed by each party. The final appraisal results of Jichengxiang Company were: under the filed contract (fixed total price contract), the total project cost was appraised at RMB 117,323,856.47; under the supplemental agreement (adjustable price contract), the total project cost was appraised at RMB 150,465,810.58. This appraisal conclusion, after multiple rounds of cross-examination and corrections by both parties, complies with legal requirements and can be used as a basis for determining the facts.

The first-instance court also found the following facts: On July 20, 2011, Jiangsu First Construction issued a project contact note to Changlong Company and the supervision unit for the project, Tangshan Sifang Engineering Construction Supervision Co., Ltd., the main content of which was to request that Changlong Company and the supervision unit confirm that the project had been idle for 81 days due to reasons attributable to Changlong Company, and that an extension of 81 days and reasonable compensation should be granted. Lu Lianfang of the supervision unit signed: "The facts are correct. Please have Party A and the contractor negotiate a reasonable solution." The supervision department affixed its seal.

The first-instance court held that the main issues in this case included: (1) how to calculate the amount of outstanding project payment and interest owed by Changlong Company; (2) how to handle the idle work losses claimed by Jiangsu First Construction; and (3) whether the counterclaims filed by Changlong Company were sustainable.

(1) Regarding the calculation of the amount of outstanding project payment and interest owed by Changlong Company. First, both construction contracts signed by the parties are invalid. The "Filed Contract" signed on December 8, 2009, although signed after tendering and bidding procedures and filed with the administrative department for construction, was preceded by a four-party review of the structural and electrical construction drawings for the project by Jiangsu First Construction, Changlong Company, the design unit, and the supervision unit, before Jiangsu First Construction was determined as the construction unit through tendering and bidding procedures. Moreover, Jiangsu First Construction had already completed part of the construction work, such as positioning surveys, foundation marking, and foundation blinding for some of the buildings. That is, there were acts that violated the prohibitive provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law, such as determining the contractor before tendering. Therefore, this filed contract should be deemed invalid. The "Supplemental Agreement" signed on December 28, 2009, was not signed through tendering and bidding procedures and materially changed the contract price stipulated in the filed contract. It falls within the scope of the "black contract" referred to in Article 21 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts (hereinafter referred to as the "Construction Contract Judicial Interpretation") and should also be deemed invalid as a matter of law. Second, the two construction contracts in this case were signed only twenty days apart. It is not possible to determine from the timeline which contract was actually performed. The parties themselves did not expressly stipulate which contract was actually performed. The contents of the two contracts, such as subcontracting by Party A and quality and price confirmation of materials, were both reflected during the performance of the contract. Moreover, the invalidity of both contracts means that the law has given a negative evaluation to both contracts. Invalid contracts have the same level of validity, and there is no issue of one being given priority over the other. Therefore, considering the circumstances of this case, the losses caused by the invalidity of the contracts can be shared by the parties in proportion to their degree of fault, in accordance with Article 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract Law"). In this case, the loss is the price difference between the two contracts, which is RMB 33,141,954.11 (RMB 150,465,810.58 - RMB 117,323,856.47). Changlong Company, as the employer, is the entity legally responsible for organizing tendering and bidding. It bears primary responsibility for failing to conduct tendering and bidding in accordance with the law. Jiangsu First Construction, as a professional construction unit with a special grade qualification, should also be well versed in the relevant provisions of the Tendering and Bidding Law. Therefore, it also bears fault for failing to conduct tendering and bidding in accordance with the law, leading to the invalidity of the contracts. A comprehensive analysis of the circumstances of this case makes it appropriate to share the losses in a ratio of 6:4. Therefore, the total project amount should be determined as RMB 137,209,028.94 (RMB 117,323,856.47 + RMB 33,141,954.11 x 60%). After deducting the project payment already paid of RMB 124,939,155, the outstanding project payment is RMB 12,269,873.94. As for the issue of interest, Changlong Company did not have a history of defaulting on progress payments during the construction process. After Jiangsu First Construction submitted the settlement documents, Changlong Company repeatedly verified the quantities of work with it. Based on the above facts, Changlong Company did not have the subjective intent to default on the project payment. The fundamental reason for the dispute over the project payment was the significant disagreement between the parties as to which contract should be used as the basis for settlement. Both parties are at fault for signing the two invalid contracts and thereby causing the dispute. Therefore, it is appropriate to calculate interest on the outstanding project payment from the date Jiangsu First Construction filed the lawsuit, at the loan interest rate of the same period announced by the People's Bank of China.

(2) Regarding the loss of work stoppage and idleness claimed by Jiangsu First Construction. In the project contact sheet dated July 20, 2011, the supervision unit had already confirmed by stamp and signature that there indeed existed a fact of 81 days of idle work by Jiangsu First Construction caused by reasons attributable to Changlong Company, but the visa sheet did not determine the amount of loss, nor did it involve a calculation method for the loss of work stoppage. Although Jiangsu First Construction also applied for an appraisal of the amount of such loss, because a considerable part of the evidence it provided for the loss of work stoppage and idleness was its own records and unilaterally provided information such as the number of workers, the name list, the wage amounts, and the on-site machinery quantities, etc., and Changlong Company did not recognize this, the court of first instance found it difficult to determine the objective authenticity of the above evidence, and it was also doubtful whether the appraisal conclusion based on this evidence could be adopted. Therefore, no appraisal was entrusted for this. In view of the fact that there had also been an 8-day work stoppage and idleness between the two parties during the previous construction process, and the compensation amount negotiated by the parties was 70,000 yuan, which basically reflected the degree of loss caused to Jiangsu First Construction by the work stoppage and idleness, based on this, the loss for the 81 days of work stoppage and idleness could be discretionarily determined to be 700,000 yuan.

(3) Regarding the quality issue of the stairwell insulation raised in Changlong Company's counterclaim. During the on-site inspection, the appraisal institution found that the thickness of the insulation layer for the partition walls between the stairwell and the unheated corridor and the residence did not meet the design requirements. This quality issue was not caused by the owner's use, but was because Jiangsu First Construction failed to construct according to the drawings during the construction process. Therefore, Jiangsu First Construction should bear the quality responsibility. Changlong Company's claim requesting Jiangsu First Construction to rectify the part with quality issues was in compliance with the provisions of Article 281 of the Contract Law and should be supported. In this case, the part of the project payment amounting to 1,972,553.25 yuan for this part was temporarily not handled, and it was to be settled separately by the parties after Jiangsu First Construction completed the rectification to a qualified standard. Therefore, the amount of outstanding project payment in this case was temporarily determined to be 10,297,320.69 yuan (12,269,873.94 yuan - 1,972,553.25 yuan). As for the losses caused by other project quality issues asserted in Changlong Company's counterclaim, although Changlong Company claimed that it had repeatedly requested Jiangsu First Construction to carry out repairs, it failed to provide evidence to support its claim. Moreover, the "Cost Summary Table" it provided to prove the amount of loss was prepared unilaterally by it, and its authenticity could not be verified. Therefore, this claim was not supported. Regarding Changlong Company's claim that it suffered losses due to Jiangsu First Construction's delay in delivering construction documents, Jiangsu First Construction argued that this was the result of its exercise of the right of defense based on Changlong Company's outstanding project payment. The court of first instance held that paying the project payment was the main contractual obligation of the developer. Under the circumstance that Changlong Company had not paid the project payment in full, Jiangsu First Construction's exercise of the right of defense was in compliance with the provisions of Article 67 of the Contract Law regarding the right to simultaneous performance defense, and did not constitute a breach of contract. Therefore, this counterclaim of Changlong Company was not supported. However, submitting completion acceptance materials is a statutory obligation of the construction unit. The fact that it enjoys the right of defense under specific circumstances does not mean that it can persistently fail to perform the obligation to deliver the completion materials. Jiangsu First Construction also recognized in the court trial that it should deliver the materials. Therefore, this claim of Changlong Company was supported. As for the issue of interest on overpaid project payment raised by Changlong Company, through the calculation of the project price and the outstanding project payment, there was no overpayment of project payment in this case. Therefore, no interest loss issue arose, and this counterclaim was also not supported.

In summary, the court of first instance made the following judgment: (1) Changlong Company shall, within fifteen days from the effective date of the judgment, pay Jiangsu First Construction the outstanding project payment of 10,297,320.69 yuan, and shall pay interest at the same period benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China from October 9, 2013, until the date of full payment; (2) Changlong Company shall, within fifteen days from the effective date of the judgment, pay Jiangsu First Construction the loss of work stoppage and idleness of 700,000 yuan; (3) Jiangsu First Construction shall, within fifteen days from the effective date of the judgment, deliver all construction documents to Changlong Company; (4) Dismiss all other claims of Jiangsu First Construction; (5) Dismiss all other counterclaims of Changlong Company.

Court acceptance fee for the principal action: 306,512 yuan; appraisal fee: 1.2 million yuan, totaling 1,506,512 yuan, to be borne by Jiangsu First Construction in the amount of 1,074,600 yuan and by Changlong Company in the amount of 431,912 yuan; Court acceptance fee for the counterclaim: 51,873 yuan, to be borne by Jiangsu First Construction in the amount of 7,492 yuan and by Changlong Company in the amount of 44,381 yuan.

This court found upon retrial that on September 28, 2016, the Jiangsu Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a Notice of Approval of Company Change Registration, and the name of Jiangsu First Construction and Installation Co., Ltd. was changed to Jiangsu First Construction and Installation Group Co., Ltd. During the second instance, the parties did not submit new evidence. This court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of the Court:
Focusing on the parties' appellate claims, factual reasons, and defense opinions, the issues in dispute in this case are: (1) Whether the original judgment was correct in determining the amount of outstanding project payment that Changlong Company should pay to Jiangsu First Construction and the interest; (2) Whether the original judgment was correct in ordering Changlong Company to pay Jiangsu First Construction the loss of work stoppage and idleness.

(1) Whether the original judgment was correct in determining the amount of outstanding project payment that Changlong Company should pay to Jiangsu First Construction and the interest.
First, regarding the basis for settling the project price involved in the case. Jiangsu First Construction appealed, arguing that the actual contract performed by the parties was the "Supplementary Agreement," and the project price should be settled accordingly. Changlong Company argued that, according to the "Judicial Interpretation on Construction Project Construction Contract Disputes," the "Supplementary Agreement" was a black contract, and the "Filing Contract" should be the basis for settling the project price.

Opinion of the Court:
First, the "Bidding Law" and the "Regulations on the Scope and Scale Standards of Construction Project Bidding Items" clearly stipulate the scope of projects subject to mandatory bidding. The construction project involved in this case was a project subject to mandatory bidding. Although the "Filing Contract" signed by the parties on December 8, 2009, was signed through a bidding process and filed with the construction administrative authority, before the bidding process determined Jiangsu First Construction as the construction unit, on the one hand, Changlong Company entrusted Jiangsu First Construction to construct the foundation pit support, which was a sub-project of the building engineering unit project; on the other hand, Jiangsu First Construction, Changlong Company, the design unit, and the supervision unit conducted a four-party joint review of the structural and electrical construction drawings involved in the project, and Jiangsu First Construction had completed the positioning measurement, foundation setting out, foundation cushion, etc. for some buildings. The court of first instance correctly found that the bidding for the project involved in the case had acts that violated the prohibitive provisions of the "Bidding Law," such as determining the party before bidding, and the "Filing Contract" was invalid.

Second, the "Supplementary Agreement" signed by the parties on December 28, 2009, was signed without going through the bidding process, and it changed the substantive contents such as the project price agreed in the filing contract. Pursuant to Article 21 of the "Judicial Interpretation on Construction Project Construction Contract Disputes," the court of first instance correctly held that the "Supplementary Agreement" was a separately concluded contract with substantive contents inconsistent with the bid-winning contract filed and thus invalid.

Third, Article 2 of the "Judicial Interpretation on Construction Project Construction Contract Disputes" provides that if a construction project construction contract is invalid, but the construction project has passed the completion acceptance, and the contractor requests payment of the project price with reference to the contract, it shall be supported. Article 21 of the same Judicial Interpretation provides that if the parties separately conclude a construction project construction contract for the same construction project, and the substantive contents are inconsistent with the filed bid-winning contract, the filed bid-winning contract shall be the basis for settling the project price. In this case, although the "Filing Contract," which was signed through the bidding process and filed with the construction administrative authority, was invalid due to violation of mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, the premise for applying Article 21 of the "Judicial Interpretation on Construction Project Construction Contract Disputes" does not exist, nor does the "Supplementary Agreement," which circumvents the bidding system and violates the substantive contents of the filed bid-winning contract, have priority in application.

Article 58 of the Contract Law provides that after a contract is invalidated or revoked, any property acquired under the contract shall be returned; if return is impossible or unnecessary, compensation shall be made at an estimated value. The party at fault shall compensate the other party for the losses suffered as a result; if both parties are at fault, each shall bear the corresponding liability. The specificity of a construction project construction contract lies in the fact that the performance of the contract is the process by which the contractor materializes labor and construction materials into the construction project. After the contract is confirmed invalid, it can only be returned by way of compensation at an estimated value. In this case, the parties claim that the project price should be paid with reference to the contract pursuant to Article 2 of the "Judicial Interpretation on Construction Project Construction Contract Disputes." Since the "Filing Contract" and the "Supplementary Agreement" provide for different settlement methods, it is first necessary to determine the contract that reflects the parties' true mutual intent and was actually performed.

Considering the "Filing Contract" and the "Supplementary Agreement" in this case, from the perspective of signing time, the "Filing Contract" was signed on December 1, 2009, and filed with the Tangshan Construction Bureau on December 30, 2009; the "Supplementary Agreement" was signed on December 28, 2009, only twenty days apart. From the perspective of agreed construction scope, the "Filing Contract" stipulated that the construction scope included the construction and installation of all civil works, plumbing, electrical, elevators, fire protection, ventilation, etc., as indicated in the construction drawings. The "Supplementary Agreement" stipulated that the construction scope included all construction and installation works of the Golden Heyuan Project, excluding earthwork excavation, ventilation and fire protection, plastic steel windows, landscaping, greenery, garage management system, security, elevators, heat exchange station equipment, distribution room equipment, and gas facilities, as well as municipal works such as rainwater and sewage, and main community loop roads. The actual construction scope was not entirely consistent with the agreements in the two contracts. From the perspective of agreed settlement price, the "Filing Contract" agreed on a fixed price; the "Supplementary Agreement" agreed to implement the Hebei Province 2008 quota and related documents, with the total construction and installation engineering cost settlement price reduced by 3%, and the "Supplementary Agreement" also agreed on price adjustment and that engineering materials would be subject to quality and price recognition by Party A. Based on the above analysis, the evidence submitted by the parties could hardly prove the facts on which their claims were based. The court of first instance correctly held that the parties had no clear agreement on the actual contract performed, and the contents of the two contracts, such as subcontracting by Party A and quality and price recognition of materials, were both reflected in the contract performance process, making it impossible to determine the actual contract performed.

When it is impossible to determine the contract that reflects the parties' true mutual intent and was actually performed, the losses caused by the invalidity of the contract should be borne by the parties according to their degree of fault based on factors such as the fault in contracting, the quality of the completed project, and the balance of interests, in accordance with Article 58 of the Contract Law. The court of first instance found that the difference between the two contracts, for which the true mutual intent and performance could not be determined, constituted the loss. Based on the fault of Changlong Company, as the developer that organized the bidding in accordance with the law, and Jiangsu First Construction, as a professional construction unit with special-grade qualifications that should also be familiar with relevant legal provisions such as the Bidding Law, combined with the fact that the project in this case had passed the completion acceptance, it was not improper for the court of first instance to have Changlong Company and Jiangsu First Construction bear the loss in a ratio of 6:4. Jiangsu First Construction's appeal claim that the project price should be settled according to the "Supplementary Agreement" lacked factual and legal basis, and this court does not support it.

Regarding the interest on the project price involved in the case, Jiangsu First Construction appealed, claiming that the interest on the project payment should be paid from January 30, 2012, at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period. The court of first instance held that Changlong Company had no default in paying the project progress payment during the construction process, nor did it have subjective malice in defaulting on the project payment. Moreover, both parties were at fault for signing the two invalid contracts and thereby causing the dispute over the settlement of the project price. Therefore, the interest on the outstanding project payment would accrue from the date of Jiangsu First Construction's filing of the lawsuit at the same period benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China. Opinion of the Court: Article 18 of the "Judicial Interpretation on Construction Project Construction Contract Disputes" provides that interest shall be calculated from the date on which the project payment becomes due. If the parties have no agreement or the agreement on the time of payment is unclear, the following times shall be deemed as the time for payment: (1) if the construction project has been actually delivered, the date of delivery; (2) if the construction project has not been delivered, the date of submission of the completion settlement documents; (3) if the construction project has not been delivered and the project price has not been settled, the date on which the party files the lawsuit. The project involved in the case passed the completion acceptance and was delivered for use on November 30, 2011. Both contracts involved in the case were found to be invalid. On the one hand, the time for payment of the project price agreed in the contract could not be applied by reference to the contract; on the other hand, the nature of interest on the developer's outstanding project payment is statutory fruits. After the construction project passes the completion acceptance and is delivered to the developer, the developer has actual control and is conditionally able to exercise possession, use, and benefit rights over the disputed construction project. Therefore, calculating the interest on the project price from the date of delivery after the project passes the completion acceptance is in line with balancing the interests of the parties. Jiangsu First Construction's claim that the interest on the project payment should be paid from January 30, 2012, at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period is supported by this court.

(2) Whether the original judgment was correct in ordering Changlong Company to pay Jiangsu First Construction the loss of work stoppage and idleness.
Jiangsu First Construction appealed, claiming that the loss of idleness should be paid based on its actual labor costs and machinery shift costs incurred. Opinion of the Court: In the project contact sheet dated July 20, 2011, involved in the case, the supervision unit had already confirmed by stamp and signature that there indeed existed a fact of 81 days of idle work by Jiangsu First Construction caused by reasons attributable to Changlong Company, but the visa sheet did not determine the amount of loss, nor did it involve a calculation method for the loss of work stoppage. A considerable part of the evidence provided by Jiangsu First Construction for the loss of work stoppage and idleness was its own records and unilaterally provided information such as the number of workers, the name list, the wage amounts, and the on-site machinery quantities, etc., and Changlong Company did not recognize this. The court of first instance, in view of the fact that there had also been an 8-day work stoppage and idleness between the parties during the previous construction process, and the compensation amount negotiated by the parties was 70,000 yuan, which basically reflected the degree of loss caused to Jiangsu First Construction by the work stoppage and idleness, discretionarily determined the loss for the 81 days of work stoppage and idleness to be 700,000 yuan, which was not obviously improper.

Additionally, Jiangsu First Construction appealed, arguing that it was improper for the first-instance judgment to deduct 1,972,553.25 yuan in advance as repair costs. Opinion of the Court: During the on-site inspection by the appraisal institution involved in the case, it was found that the thickness of the insulation layer for the partition walls between the stairwell and the unheated corridor and the residence did not meet the design requirements. This quality issue was not caused by the owner's use, but was because Jiangsu First Construction failed to construct according to the drawings during the construction process. Therefore, Jiangsu First Construction should bear the quality responsibility. The first-instance judgment correctly held that Changlong Company's request for Jiangsu First Construction to rectify the part with quality issues and that the project payment of 1,972,553.25 yuan for this part be temporarily not handled, to be settled separately by the parties after Jiangsu First Construction completes the rectification to a qualified standard, was not improper.

Jiangsu First Construction appealed, claiming that the judgment should be changed to order Changlong Company to deliver all construction documents to it within 15 days from the date of full payment of the outstanding amount. Opinion of the Court: Submitting completion acceptance materials is a statutory obligation of the construction unit. The fact that it enjoys the right of defense under specific circumstances does not mean that it can persistently fail to perform the obligation to deliver the completion materials. Moreover, Jiangsu First Construction also recognized in the first-instance trial that it should deliver the materials. Therefore, the first-instance judgment ordering Jiangsu First Construction to deliver all construction documents to Changlong Company within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment was not improper.

In summary, Jiangsu First Construction's appeal claims are partially sustained. Pursuant to Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. Affirm Items 2, 3, and 5 of the civil judgment (2013) Ji Min Yi Chu Zi No. 17 of Hebei High People's Court;
2. Reverse Item 4 of the civil judgment (2013) Ji Min Yi Chu Zi No. 17 of Hebei High People's Court;
3. Amend Item 1 of the civil judgment (2013) Ji Min Yi Chu Zi No. 17 of Hebei High People's Court to read: Tangshan Changlong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall, within fifteen days from the effective date of this judgment, pay Jiangsu First Construction and Installation Group Co., Ltd. the outstanding project payment of 10,297,320.69 yuan, and shall pay interest at the same period benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China from January 30, 2012, until the date of full payment;
4. Dismiss all other claims of Jiangsu First Construction and Installation Group Co., Ltd.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the interest on the debt for the delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
